column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check
Article dates the empire from the mid 3rd century to the mid 6th; the entry says fourth to sixth century. The text gives no start date for the empire as a whole.
Four sections used; Legacy short. Article says Rouran lasted from late 4th century to mid 6th; consistent with entry.

Article says the viceroyalty/State of India began 1505 with Almeida; entry says viceroy based at Goa from 1530 (the article gives 1530 as the move of capital from Cochin). Consistent. Entry mentions Ethiopia/Adal; article text given does not, so omitted.
SKIPPED: article is under 300 words, mostly a list of tributaries and dams; adds little to the description

Entry says the Iazyges settled between Danube and Tisza in the early first century CE; article says c. 44 BC. Entry says Domitian war and 5,500 horsemen sent to Britain after defeat in 175; article gives peace in 179 and does not mention Britain or Domitian. Left these points out.

Article calls him "caliph" in places (inaccurate); text avoids. Zaida of Seville material (daughter or daughter-in-law) left out as disputed. Article spells the son Rasid/Rashid; used al-Rashid and Rashid as given.
Entry says Islam adopted in 9th and 10th centuries; article gives Zaidi in the 9th century and Isma'ilism from the 10th. Consistent.
SKIPPED: article is about 400 words, with the regional sections empty; too little beyond the description

Entry says written about 250 BCE (article: dated c. 250 BC on palaeography; the linen itself carbon-dated 390 BC +/- 45). Both given with attribution. Article also says Brugsch in 1877 and Richard Burton episode; omitted.
SKIPPED: article is under 300 words and the description already carries its main facts

Article gives his rule as c. 1816 to 1831 and seizure of Baghdad 1816-1817; entry says 1817 to 1831. Text avoids a single start year. Entry says plague and floods helped the Ottoman army and printing works; article says neither. Article says "the Sultan seized back control at British instigation" — attributed as account.
Article says text survives in four papyrus fragments (184 columns); entry says a single papyrus in Berlin; text avoids a count of fragments.
Entry says established under Emperor Wu in 124 BCE; the article gives no founding date or founder, only the Han dynasty. Omitted.
SKIPPED: article is under 270 words; adds little to the description
None.

Entry says he resisted Persians as governor of Sohar in the 1740s and was elected imam; article gives 1749 election. Zanzibar rule until 1964 in entry not in article; omitted. Article says "Imam" election 1749 but also Persians arrived in 1737; consistent with entry.

Article covers only geography, climate and vegetation; the entry's kingdoms and Fons are not in it, so omitted. Article treats Western High Plateau as the same place as Bamenda Grassfields; entry equates Grassfields with North-West and West regions, article names only the West Region for Dschang.

Article gives death 9 Sept 1958 in the lead and 10 Sept in the Death section: left as 'September 1958'. Article attributes pearling collapse to earlier causes and calls the Mikimoto/Depression narrative disputed; entry says collapse in the 1930s: I used the article's decline from about 1910 without naming a decade of collapse. Entry says 'drawing merchants from Persia' - consistent. Article oddly credits the 1934/1937 aviation and oil agreements to 'Sheikh Rashid'; I wrote 'an agreement for flights ... and an oil concession' without naming who signed. The 1937 oil agreement is described as preliminary; I wrote 'in outline'.

Article is Dervish War; the supplied text is truncated, so Hassan's death and the details of the Taleh fall are not in it and were left out. Article says Dervish capital was Taleh. Entry says 'several British, Ethiopian and Italian expeditions'; article says five British expeditions. Article's lead says a peace treaty-protectorate period from 1905.

Article's own dates are consistent with the entry (2600-2000 BCE). Article says Iraqi excavations 'in 1975' and also 'between 1970 and 1975': left vague as 'in 1975' for the one season. Article mentions an 'Aryan invasion' as a cause of collapse: omitted as contested.

Article disagrees with itself and the entry on the end of the capital: 814-968 vs 972-73 for the Rashtrakuta capital; the Chalukyas 'remained capital until about 1050' (entry says they moved to Kalyani); a claim that Rajendra Chola destroyed it in 1007. I left the Chalukya move and the Chola destruction out and kept only the 972-73 sack. 'Reported to have ruled from it' for the Chalukyas is loose; revise if the editor prefers. Article gives 2001 census population 11,180: omitted as dated.

Article dates death to summer 1795; entry says 1796 - left the year out. Article says Nasr Al-Madhkur was appointed by the Zands; entry says he served the sheikhs of Bushehr - I wrote only 'governor of Bahrain'. Article says he 'blockaded Al Zubarah the previous year' in one place and 1783 elsewhere. Article says five children but lists four: not stated.

Article gives Babullah's birth as traditionally 10 Feb 1528 but possibly much later: left out. Article says Hairun r. 1535-1570. Article states Portuguese stayed besieged 'five years' and left 15 July 1575; entry says surrendered 1575: consistent. Article says Gowa conversion in 1605 vs Ternatan tradition: not told. The article's lead calls him 'the greatest Sultan': judgement omitted.

Article calls Maktoum joint founder and first ruler with Obeid and says he took over entirely in 1836; entry says he ruled 1833-1852 and founded the dynasty. I told the 1833 migration and the 1836 sole rule without a start date for his rule. Article says he signed the truces after Obeid's 1835 one; entry says 'from 1835'. Article's 1843 truce is called ten-year. Article calls the 1843 truce 'Maritime Truce' and the 1853 one perpetual. Article names Saeed bin Butti as his brother and successor (brother in the Buraimi episode).

Article names his wife Saint Ermenburga in one place and Domne Eafe in the legend; entry says Eafe. Article says 'Mildgið'; I spelt 'Mildgyth' (not in file: spelling variant, check). Article: Chronicle 'implies' Penda was father; Kentish legend states it. Article thin (about 390 words); 'The saints of this family were venerated' is the entry's own statement.

Article's lead says Nasrat contended with the Mughals 'by 1526 in the Battle of Ghaghra', but the body dates it 6 May 1529: used 1529. Entry says he 'lost' at Ghaghra; article says Mughals victorious and he sued for peace. Article uses 'Nasrat'; entry 'Nusrat'. Entry says Qadam Rasul shrine built by him; article only mentions it as near his burial: not stated.
SKIPPED: article has about 250 words in all and adds little beyond the existing description Article gives c. 1504 - c. 1550 for the reign and Esigie's wife Elaba supporting him until c. 1547.

Entry says the battle was on 17 January and the royalists numbered about 6,000; article says 'January 1811', Calleja arrived 16 January and had 5,000 to 8,000 men: I gave neither a battle day nor a count of the royalists (wrote 'a few thousand'). Article puts the battle 60 km east of Guadalajara; entry says near Guadalajara. Article contradicts itself on the insurgents' command: Allende at the bridge in one place, Hidalgo named first in the lead.

Article gives birth as 1794 (entry c. 1794) and her age as 16 at death. Court Journal 1835 prose version differs (she survives poison then is stabbed): not told. Article's Amir Khan account says she drank the poison herself, while the Asiatic Annual Register says her aunt administered it: I gave the register's version only.

Entry's description (from the Gupta Empire profile) says it was compiled or refined during the Gupta period; article says only 100 BCE-400 CE, no decisive conclusion. I stated the article's range and did not mention the Gupta period. Article's sigla D, P and NMS replaced by plain descriptions.

Article gives his reign as 1436-1459 and also 'twenty-four years', and 'over twenty years'; entry says c. 1435-1459: I gave no start year for the reign, only Shamsuddin's death in 1435 or 1436. Entry's 1487 end of dynasty by Abyssinian guards is not in the article: omitted. Article says he was 'formerly a farmer'.
Article's lead says Krishna III honoured him; entry same. Article also lists Gatapratiagata (lost; language uncertain): omitted. Entry says 'tenth century'; article c. 945: consistent.

Article calls him 'Anantivarman' once (slip) and names a poet 'Ranakar' and 'Ananvardhana' and the scholar 'Anandhavardana': the last two likely both Anandavardhana; I printed the article's spellings. Article says date of death 11 June 883; I wrote 883. Article claims Suyya's river works made the Jhelum meet the Indus; I told as the article does. 'survives from his building' is an inference from the article's line that he built the Avantiswami Temple: harmless but note.

Article says he is sometimes identified with Kudakko Nedum Cheralathan: stated as 'some sources'. Entry says father of Senguttuvan, hero of the Silappatikaram; article gives Chenkuttuvan as son and says nothing about the epic: I used only the article's name. Entry omits date; article fl. c. 155 CE.
Entry says Kallar identity took shape from late 18th century (Bayly); consistent. Article mixes 'palaiyakarars' spellings; used palaiyakkarars.
Entry says Poligar Wars 1799-1805; article says 1798-1805 and also 1799 for the first war; I avoided giving a start year for the wars as a whole and gave only the Second War 1800-1805.

Article says 'killed two soldiers on morning of April 2' and, in aftermath, 'April 1967' start; consistent. Article says killing of 19 rebels and 'nearly 200 captured'. Entry says Lon Nol army suppressed; article says he resigned end April then returned in 1968; I kept both. 'severed heads' bounty omitted as 'allegedly' beyond attribution; kept 'said to have'. Article's Chinese dominance claims omitted.

Article does not describe Velama as 'Telugu-speaking landholding community' or warrior families under Kakatiya as fact; it hedges (Talbot). Desc says 'Velama warrior families served the Kakatiya dynasty' and Recherla Velamas ruled; article notes Velama designation did not exist as consolidated category in Recherla period. I avoided calling the Recherla 'Velamas' and recorded the tension here.
Article does not state it was 'one of the largest' irrigation works of a princely state; not repeated.
SKIPPED: Article has about 300 words of substance, mostly one legend; adds little beyond the entry.

Desc says Kokni is related to Marathi and Konkani and that they live in the Dangs; article does not give language; not repeated. 'Legacy' used for religion and festival; 'Organisation and way of life' is thin.

Heading 'Death and legacy' used though his death is not told in the article; change to 'Legacy' if flagged. Article: defeat at Vallala 916 by Parantaka (after Krishna's reign per entry r. to 914) - omitted. Article says Krishna III in Altekar passage - omitted. Article gives Gunabhadra/Lokasena claim.

Article gives the founding as 1707 (lead, with 'Meteka') and 1698 (History); entry says early 18th century. I gave no founding year. Article's lead says capital moved from Garhgaon; entry says 'main royal seat'. Article does not mention Jorhat or the 1769 seizure as such; I said 'occupied on many occasions'.
SKIPPED: Article under 280 words, with disputed identification of the site; too thin.

Entry says ruling Maharaj Rana 'from 1911'; article agrees (succession 1911, full powers 1913). Article says his daughter married Pratap Singh of Nabha in 1943; omitted. Article says Matsya merged with 'Greater Rajasthan to form the United State of Rajasthan' 15 May 1949; entry says 1949 into Rajasthan.

Entry says Futa Toro Imamate 1776 and Bundu; article gives same. Article's Sokoto 1808 (entry silent). Article says Futa Jallon imamate 'first Muslim state founded by the Fulbe'; omitted. Article: Torodbe 'from at least 17th to early 20th century'.
Entry mentions Bagyendanwa drum and Haya kingdoms; article does not, so omitted. Entry says 'c. 15th century'; article's 1430-1446 is consistent. 'Legacy' used since no death is told.

Entry places the papyri in the reign of Amenemhat III; the article names no king for the despatches (only Senusret I and III for the forts; regnal 'year 3'). Left the reign out. Article's sentence 'Senusret I started to push south' kept as given.

Entry calls him 'king of Uí Maine ... d. 1014'; article consistent. Article's O'Donovan passage dates his chiefship to 1003; the article says he succeeded Muirgus (killed 986) - not reconciled, I stated both as the article gives them but attributed 1003 to the annals. Entry says Brian's Battle of Clontarf; article says Dublin in 1014.

Article contradicts itself: says Mpondomise are 'not Nguni' yet 'part of the Nguni people'; entry says southern Nguni. Left Nguni classification out. Article says kingdom existed 'over 800 years' and 'thousands of years' - omitted. Article calls revolt 1880-81, entry says lost independence to the Cape Colony after the 1880 revolt; article says Union of South Africa removed status in 1904 - I followed article. Genealogy with invented-looking dates (1120 etc.) omitted. Several passages of the article are partisan; Bhaca described as 'backward' omitted.
SKIPPED: Article about 270 words with little detail; also dates differ (1835 vs entry c. 1836).
